result.summary: Replaces standard smart pointers with `NotNull` wrappers for pointers guaranteed never to be null, specifically the return value of `CreateNewBlock` and internal pimpl member pointers. It adds unit tests for `NotNull` semantics and eliminates redundant runtime null checks on callers.
result.problem: Pointers that can never be null are represented as standard nullable smart pointers, obscuring API contracts from developers. This leads to inconsistent call-site checks and dead error-handling branches that clutter test coverage and mutation testing reports.
evidence: PR description: 'Pointers that are never null still have confusing null checks (with possible error handling return branches), which are always dead in coverage reports or when applying mutation testing.'
Commit messages cite review suggestions from PR #34844 for both NotNull tests and pimpl annotations.
result.scope_notes: The diff was not provided in the patch payload; changes span 20 files across block template creation, IPC, and test suites.
result.card: Replaces nullable smart pointers with NotNull wrappers for block generation via CreateNewBlock and various pimpl member pointers, accompanied by new NotNull unit tests. Currently, callers cannot tell from function signatures whether pointers can be null, leading to inconsistent and dead null checks in error handling branches. The author notes that enforcing non-nullness at compile-time eliminates dead branches from test coverage reports and clarifies pointer semantics. No dependencies are declared.
uncertainties: Full diff was omitted, so exact call sites and removed branches cannot be independently verified.

risk.why: A mistake in pointer lifetime or unexpected null dereference inside NotNull wrapper initialization could trigger an assertion abort or crash during block template creation.
